Why go: Samui's classic sights in one morning

Most of Koh Samui's best-known landmarks sit on the north and east coasts, 20–40 minutes apart by road. Seeing them by taxi means negotiating each leg; on a scooter it means riding the busy ring road between Chaweng and Lamai. A shared minivan with a guide strings them together in a morning and has you back at the hotel by early afternoon.

What you'll do

The tour starts at Wat Plai Laem, with its many-armed Guan Yin statue on a lake, then the Big Buddha on its causeway island. From the Lad Koh viewpoint you look down over Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove, then continue to Hin Ta and Hin Yai, the rock formations south of Lamai. The last stop is Na Muang 1, where the pool at the base is a short walk from the car park. With the elephant option you also spend about half an hour at a non-riding elephant camp.

Who it suits

  • First-time visitors who want an overview of the island early in their stay.
  • Families with children: the stops are short and the van is air-conditioned.
  • Anyone who doesn't want to ride a scooter on the ring road.

Who should choose something else

  • Wheelchair users and anyone who struggles with steps.
  • Travellers who want the rough tracks and hilltop viewpoints: a jeep safari adds the Secret Buddha Garden and the 4x4 roads.
  • Groups of 5 or more may prefer a private van with driver and their own pace.

Good to know

  • Temples: cover shoulders and knees, take shoes off where asked and don't point your feet at Buddha images.
  • Waterfall: rocks around Na Muang are slippery; the falls are fullest from October to January and can be thin in April and May.
  • Heat: the stops are mostly in sun between 10:00 and 13:00, so bring water and a hat.
